filming.route: Koror State commercial photography licence (Koror and the Rock Islands), plus permits from each other state filmed in
filming.detail: Koror State Law K8-202-2008: commercial still photography needs a 10-day licence of US$100 (about A$142 at US$0.7040, 30 October 2026); motion picture permits are set by the Governor case by case. News media are exempt. Other states are reported to need their own permits.
filming.next: Ask the Koror State Government, then each state you plan to film in.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are strict. Long sentences apply for possessing illegal 'hard drugs'. Hard drugs include heroin, cocaine and synthetics.
laws.heading: Drug laws

laws.rule: A traditional bul (decree by traditional leadership) is in effect in Koror and Airai. This decree is a curfew in place between midnight and 5am in the hamlets (suburbs) to reduce petty crime related to drug use. A similar measure is in effect in the states of Ngarchelong and Ngiwal. Foreigners are unlikely to be the target of these measures and application is inconsistent. However, it is still recommended that you follow the advice of local authorities and have a genuine reason to be in these areas during these times. The legal drinking age is 21 years. laws.rule: To drive in Palau for up to 30 days, you may need: an International Driving Permit (IDP) a valid Australian driver's licence You must get your IDP before you arrive. After 30 days, you must get a local licence.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the US Dollar (USD). ATMs are available in larger centres and at the airport. Most shops in Palau accept credit cards. Some shops will only accept cash. Check with the shop in advance or have both payment options available.
